title: Doomers Will Always Have Small Backs
summary: NH responds to a YouTuber's video arguing that Instagram physiques are fake. He agrees with the facts but attacks the 'black pill' conclusion: using fake social media or natural status as an excuse lowers your standards and kills progress. Self-esteem comes from building something worth being proud of, through aesthetic-focused training and action.
claims: Social media physiques are illusions: pump, flexing, perfect lighting and the single best shot out of hundreds
NH's own Instagram photos look very different from how he looks on camera in normal light
Comparing your unpumped mirror reflection to curated pictures is bad for mental health
Influencers now openly post good-vs-bad-angle comparisons, but knowing pictures are doctored does not undo the effect of constant exposure
Recognizing social media is fake is good; using it as an excuse for your lack of results is a black-pill cope
If you are small it is not because you are natural but because you have not trained enough, long enough, or correctly; you can be big and natural
Naturals who use natty status as an excuse are as harmful as fake natties: one raises standards unrealistically, the other lowers them to mediocrity
There is no pride in being natural and small; natural is your base state, you must build something to earn it
Believing everything online is fake is as damaging as believing everything is real; both create unrealistic standards
NH can vouch for natural peers who are as big as or bigger than him and look great in natural lighting
Aiming low guarantees the lowest result; with high standards even the worst case still looks good
Claims like 3D shoulders, abs or 18-inch arms being impossible naturally are worse than chasing an enhanced standard
You cannot talk yourself into being proud or love a body you dislike; pride comes only from building something worth loving
Body positivity does not work because it offers no solution, unlike changing the thing you dislike
A minimalist strength routine will not build an aesthetic physique; people who train for aesthetics get more aesthetic bodies
Many unhappy lifters are 'strength copers' who train for strength without passion, then call natural aesthetic physiques unrealistic
The claim that 5-6 years of proper training and diet could produce no aesthetic change is delusional
NH believes he could drastically improve the YouTuber's physique in one year with an aesthetic-based routine
The difference between those who make it and those who do not is belief in your ability to improve
Better to try and fail 15 times than never try; doomers avoid attempts to protect their ego
Exposure channels (and non-fitness creators claiming everyone is on PEDs) black-pill a whole generation before they even start
Fake natties destroy self-esteem in order to sell programs and supplements
NH started skinny and is now jacked, proof that building a big back naturally is possible
